study_identification.title: Atypical maturation of the functional connectome hierarchy in autism

study_characteristics.study_objective: Investigate developmental abnormalities of the cortical functional connectome hierarchy in ASD using normative modeling to quantify age-related trajectories and individual-level deviations (centile scores), and test network-level mechanisms and clinical relevance.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Hierarchy score correlated with SRS total and five subscores (awareness, cognition, communication, motivation, mannerisms); significant negative correlations overall; ABIDE-I subset non-significant likely due to smaller N.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: ASD shows atypical, nonlinear maturation of the cortical hierarchy: delayed in childhood, catch-up in adolescence, and decline in young adulthood; sensory/attention networks deviate early, DMN shows persistent impairment; hierarchy score relates to symptom severity.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Using rs-fMRI gradients (Schaefer-200), normative GAMLSS (SHASH) models trained on HCP-D and transferred to ABIDE revealed age-related expansion of the principal gradient in TD. ASD exhibited increased gradient values in sensory/attention networks and reduced values in DMN, with centile scores confirming network-specific abnormalities across developmental stages. A derived hierarchy score captured inverted-U patterns and distinguished ASD vs TD across stages. Replication in ABIDE-II and sensitivity analyses (parcellation, thresholds, handedness, motion covariate) supported robustness. Mediation analyses implicated reduced DMN segregation as a contributor to atypical hierarchy development.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Uneven age distribution, especially fewer older participants, limits trajectory characterization; cross-sectional primary analyses may not capture individual longitudinal changes; GAMLSS complexity/overfitting considerations; limited longitudinal sample size.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: Centile scoring and hierarchy score provide individualized deviation quantification; potential utility for stratification and tracking severity; cross-dataset transfer suggests feasibility for broader application after calibration.

general_notes.general_notes: Gradients estimated via BrainSpace; Procrustes alignment to group template; connectivity sparsified at 10% per row; ComBat used to mitigate ABIDE site effects; ABIDE preprocessing via QuNex adapting HCP pipelines; motion scrubbing not performed; HCP-D acquisition parameters (3T Siemens Prisma) detailed. Handedness tested (no effect). Sensitivity: thresholds 5%/10%/20%, parcellation (Glasser), and motion covariate. Potential minor inconsistency in HCP-D sex counts likely due to OCR; reported as-is.
